pr_title: Fix the word wrapping in formatting to handle escape sequences properly
pr_body:
<!-- Anything that looks like this is a comment and can't be seen after the Pull Request is created. -->

# PR Summary

Fix #17261
Fix the word wrapping in formatting to handle escape sequences properly.
The changes are mainly in 3 utility methods to take into account possible escape sequences when manipulate strings:
- `SplitLines`: split a multi-line string. Make sure the escape sequences are kept for all lines after the splitting.
- `GetWords`: split a single-line string into words. Make sure all escape sequences are kept for each word, so the decoration to the individual words is the same as they are in the string.
- `GenerateLinesWithWordWrap`. When splitting a word across multiple lines, make sure all escape sequences are kept in the same order for all individual sub-strings, so the decoration to the sub-strings is the same as they are in the original string.

Here are some examples to demonstrate the fix:

**Multi-line string in list view**

```pwsh
$m = [pscustomobject] @{ b = "`e[33mPowerShell is a task automation and configuration management program from Microsoft.`nIt consists of a command-line shell and the associated scripting language" }
$m | Format-List
```
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/127450/167923668-8799bfbf-1a3e-4bd2-87cd-37bab7d0e5e4.png)


**Multi-line string in list view with word wrapping**
```pwsh
$PSStyle.OutputRendering = 'Ansi'
$m = [pscustomobject] @{ b = "`e[33mPowerShell is a task `e[31mautomation and configuration`e[33m management program from Microsoft.`nIt consists of a command-line shell and the associated scripting language" }
$m | Format-List | Out-String -Width 45
```
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/127450/167923543-d6b930df-136d-47bc-9c62-750e93a29817.png)

**Long word across multiple lines**
```pwsh
$PSStyle.OutputRendering = 'Ansi'
$m = [pscustomobject] @{ b = "`e[33mC:\repos\PowerShell\src\`e[31mpowershell-win-core`e[33m\bin\Debug\net7.0\win7-x64\publish\pwsh.exe"; vv = "Hello world" }
$m | Format-List | Out-String -Width 40
```
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/127450/167924218-b6c6f6a8-0a06-43c2-a4e3-c746ff660102.png)

### Prerequisites

- [X] Refer to [Differences between Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell](https://docs.microsoft.com/powershell/scripting/whats-new/differences-from-windows-powershell).

### Steps to reproduce

Quote from https://github.com/PowerShell/PowerShell/issues/16700#issuecomment-1103474523:

> Technically, Format-List is not affected by this, but colors don't work there either, because when it wraps, the second line gets no formatting, which is _really **gross**_: 

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/192942/164153654-827ca3b5-fdcf-4439-9673-0b66be0a8d26.png)

And this is done by resizing the window to make the list rendering need to do word wrapping. See https://github.com/PowerShell/PowerShell/issues/16700#issuecomment-1117601312 for details.

### Expected behavior

```console
The wrapped words should keep the same color decoration.
```


### Actual behavior

```console
The wrapped words lost their color decoration.
```

```console
N/A
```

review_comments: Why do we skip vt sequence if the line ends with delimiter and vt sequence?

Because in that case the last word/line will consist of VT sequences only, with no actual character to be rendered. To the formatting system, it's the same as an empty string, so we just skip to avoid unneeded string allocations.
You think about formatting codes only but there are non-formatting codes too like OSC 2 - set windows title.
What is OSC 2? And how does that go through the formatting code here? Can you show a couple examples where this is a problem?
OSC 2 is "set windows title". I want to say VT sequences are not only formatting but control codes too.

For the "set title" control sequence in particular, the syntax is: [`ESC]2;stringBEL`](https://tldp.org/HOWTO/Xterm-Title-3.html), so there is no point to keep the VT sequence if `stringBEL` part doesn't exist.

In general, you shouldn't expect control sequences to work with PowerShell formatting. Formatting by definition is just for visualizing objects, and in my opinion, accidentally making a control sequence take effect is an unwanted side effect of the formatting, but that's inevitable today given that our `AnsiRegex` cannot tell VT sequences for visual effects from other VT sequences.
I don't understand the original intention - if we shouldn't break the line why do we break? Have we tests for the scenario?
Honestly, I don't understand either. I just tried to keep the same logic to avoid any breaking changes.
I think it is minor bug. Could you please open tracking issue so that we can discuss this later?

This is used some times too but I am not sure we can move this in ValueStringDecorated.

```suggestion
                if (vtRanges?.TryGetValue(i, out int len))
```

I don't think this check plus the if block should be moved to a utility method, as the logic is very specific to the calling context.
Also, the `== true` is required as `vtRanges` could be null.
See my reply in the below comment.

Nit: The use of IsDecorated seems unwarranted. Rather, it should be an internal implementation of ValueStringDecorated.

(In general, if now PowerShell Formatting System is based on VT sequences all string sent to it should be ValueStringDecorated.)

> (In general, if now PowerShell Formatting System is based on VT sequences all string sent to it should be ValueStringDecorated.)

I don't think that is necessary, or I should say I don't see the benefit from doing that so far.
I think we can discuss about your idea in https://github.com/PowerShell/PowerShell/issues/16643, where I think we can think again if the support to `$PSStyle` can all happen in formatting code, without having each host to do anything.

> I think we can discuss about your idea in #16643

Is it right link? I don't see my comment there.
And yes, my proposal was to move all formatting (and path case normalization) codes to formatting system.

I left a comment there about this topic: https://github.com/PowerShell/PowerShell/issues/16643#issuecomment-996984580
But it may be a better idea to open a new issue just about that, if one doesn't exist yet.
